P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes. Zambia abolished exchange-control monitoring in March 2014, and funds move freely. Since 26 Dec 2025, the Bank of Zambia Currency Directives require domestic transactions (payments to Zambian residents) to be settled in kwacha, though contracts may still be denominated in foreign currency. Payments from foreign clients to a Zambian freelancer are not domestic transactions under that definition.

P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Bank accounts may be held in local or foreign currency. Over-the-counter cash withdrawals are capped at USD 5,000 per transaction, and cash over USD 5,000 must be declared when carried across the border.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: Simplest: register a business name with PACRA (Patents and Companies Registration Agency) as a sole proprietor, using BN Form III, online or at a PACRA office. There is no minimum capital and liability is unlimited. Fees were not confirmed officially.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: A TPIN (Taxpayer Identification Number) from the Zambia Revenue Authority, obtained online or at a ZRA office with the National Registration Card (NRC). It is separate from PACRA registration.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Zambia taxes on a source basis: Zambian-source income is taxable, and residents are also taxed on foreign interest and dividends. Small businesses with turnover up to K5m can pay turnover tax at 5% of gross sales; the late-payment penalty is cut to 0.5% under the 2026 Budget. Personal income tax runs up to 37% for 2026.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Standard VAT 16%. Registration is required when taxable turnover exceeds K800,000 a year or K200,000 in any three consecutive months, so turnover-tax payers above K800,000 may also need VAT registration. Exports of goods and services are typically zero-rated, EXCEPT services physically performed in Zambia, which are standard-rated whatever the customer's residence. Smart Invoice e-invoicing applies.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021. Anyone controlling or processing personal data must register as a data controller or processor (s. 19). The Office of the Data Protection Commissioner is operational and set a registration deadline of 30 April 2025. Failing to register is an offence (fine up to ZMW 200,000 and/or up to 5 years' imprisonment). Cross-border transfers are regulated (Part X).

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: Consumer-protection / e-commerce rules for online sales (refunds, disclosures)
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Under the Electronic Communications and Transactions Act 2021, consumers may cancel an electronic transaction without reason or penalty within seven days of receiving goods, or within seven days of concluding a services agreement (s. 66). Exceptions include personalised goods and goods that deteriorate quickly. If the supplier fails its information duties, the consumer may cancel within fourteen days of receipt (s. 65(3)). Orders not executed within 30 days can be cancelled on seven days' notice (s. 67).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (4) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
